title: This Shark Was Swimming Before the Pilgrims Landed (Probably)
youtube_description:
It might be older than the United States. The Greenland shark is the longest-lived vertebrate we know of.

In 2016, researchers dated the eye lenses of 28 sharks. The biggest came out at roughly 392 years — but the honest range is 272 to 512. Headlines quote the top of that range; the study itself doesn't.

They grow about a centimetre a year and may not breed until they're 150.

Subscribe for the true version of the stories everyone half-remembers.

Sources: Nielsen et al., Science (2016).
